we proposed a novel method for recognizing complex human actions that handles missing data, that integrates privileged information in a probabilistic framework, and that employs a self-training procedure for automatic selection of the regularization parameter.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we proposed a novel supervised probabilistic approach for recognizing complex human activity that integrates LUPI in the HCRF model.
the HCRF+, which is an extension of the HCRF, is able to handle missing data and noise by using a robust Student's \text{t}-distribution.
our proposed model, HCRF+, is able to achieve the highest accuracy among all the state-of-the-art methods on all the four challenging datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HCRF+, which is trained using the maximum likelihood criterion, outperforms all the other methods in all the considered datasets.
the proposed HCRF+ method is a robust and effective approach for recognizing complex human activity in the presence of missing data during testing.
privileged information can be used to improve the performance of a model, even if the privileged information itself is noisy and incomplete.
